text: Prayer puts God in His place as the Giver, and you in yours as the receiver.
explanation:
Some people think of prayer as hard work, a way of earning God's attention. But prayer is simply coming to the One who loves to give and holding out your hands. "You do not have because you do not ask."

God already knows what you need, yet He delights to be asked, the way a father loves his child's requests. So pray for protection, for your children, for wisdom and provision, even for small things. Nothing is too big for Him, and nothing is too small to bring.

text: Melchizedek's first words to Abraham were a blessing. His is a priesthood of blessing only, and Jesus is a priest for ever in his order.
explanation:
Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, came out to meet Abraham with bread and wine, and said, "Blessed be Abram of God Most High." Under the law, the Levitical priests pronounced both blessings and curses. Melchizedek pronounced only blessing.

"The Lord has sworn and will not relent: 'You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.'" Jesus' priestly ministry for you today isn't after the order of Aaron, but of Melchizedek: King of righteousness, King of peace, whose word over you is blessing.

text: Communion proclaims the Lord's death until He comes. Hebrews says the tithe is a witness that He lives.
explanation:
"Here mortal men receive tithes, but there He receives them, of whom it is witnessed that He lives." The Levitical priests who received tithes in the temple all died. But the One Melchizedek pictures receives them in heaven, and He lives by the power of an endless life.

Abraham met Melchizedek with his hands full, and so did Melchizedek: one brought bread and wine, the other a tenth of the spoils. Salvation is coming to God with empty hands; worship is coming to Him with full ones. When you give, give with a sense of His love, thanking Him for all He's given you.

text: When Jacob saw the wagons Joseph had sent, his spirit revived, and he was called Israel again.
explanation:
For years Jacob grieved over Joseph, believing he was dead. When his sons came home saying, "Joseph is still alive, and he is governor over all the land of Egypt," his heart went numb: he couldn't believe it. But when he heard Joseph's words and saw the wagons Joseph had sent to carry him, "the spirit of Jacob their father revived."

The very next verse calls him Israel: "It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive." The good things God puts in your life are wagons from Someone who is alive and reigning. Let them strengthen your faith, and let others see them too.

text: Abraham's servant took ten camels, "for all his master's goods were in his hand." In Scripture, ten stands for the whole.
explanation:
How could all of Abraham's great wealth be in one servant's hand? Because the ten camels represented it all. Likewise, Joseph couldn't send the whole land of Egypt to his father, so he sent ten donkeys "loaded with the good things of Egypt" as a token of it all. Ten commandments represent the whole law; break one and you've broken all.

That's the principle Paul draws on: "If the firstfruit is holy, the lump is also holy." When the first tenth is set apart to the Lord, the rest is sanctified too. It's not that God needs your money; it's that He wants to bless all of it.

text: The first time "tithe" appears in the Bible, "rich" appears in the same chapter. Abraham refused to let Sodom say, "I made Abram rich."
explanation:
Right after Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything, the king of Sodom offered him all the goods he had recovered. Abraham refused: "I will take nothing, from a thread to a sandal strap… lest you should say, 'I have made Abram rich.'"

Abraham knew where his blessing came from, and he wasn't going to give that credit to anyone else. The God who received his tithe was the God who would make him rich. Your provision doesn't depend on the world's favours or the world's economy, but on the One who blesses you.

text: Under grace, you don't have to give. You get to.
explanation:
Abraham tithed to Melchizedek long before the law of Moses was given; it was a response of faith, not a commandment. Jesus told the Pharisees that justice and the love of God came first, "without leaving the others undone." Love is the motive; giving is its natural expression.

"Do not forget to do good and to share, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased." If God can be grieved, He can also be gladdened, and a generous heart gladdens Him. Give not out of fear or pride, but because you've seen how much He loves you.
